problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2}+x?$
worked_solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(-2,-1),(-2,-2),$ and $(1,1).$

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-2,-1)}=(-2)^{2}+(-2)=2, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-2,-2)}=(-2)^{2}+(-2)=2, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,1)}=(1)^{2}+(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following:
